ops.title: Flaky under load: TestRunSettlementOverrunTerminalizesClaimAndSignalsWatcher — post-terminal Run races context canceled vs ErrClosed
ops.description:
Two occurrences, both with the diff-under-test provably unrelated to worker/:

1. CI run 30205217360 (ubuntu-latest, commit c11b7f6 — the v0.20.7 staging/deployment changes, which worker does not import): pool_test.go:702 `post-terminal Run = {...}, worker: canceled / context canceled, want ErrClosed`, alongside the routine deferred-untrack WARNs. Every other package green; worker was green on both adjacent main commits (85d53fd, 08de66c).

2. Local (2026-07-26, machine carrying the agent fleet): the same worker package failed on a full-suite run under load and passed immediately in isolation (same session that proved the daemon trust-probe flake at base, task 243d40cc).

Shape: after a settlement overrun terminalizes the claim, a post-terminal Run is expected to observe ErrClosed, but under load/runner variance a context-cancellation path wins the race and surfaces `worker: canceled` instead. This is an expected-error nondeterminism between two shutdown paths — possibly a test-only ordering assumption, possibly a real ambiguity in which error post-terminal callers see. Same load-sensitive family as 243d40cc (daemon trust-probe) and fusekit 6f39134/14e1678; deserves a deliberate look at the post-terminal error contract, not a blind timeout bump.

ops.text: worker-package settlement-overrun tests pass -race -count=5 on loaded machines and shared CI runners, with the post-terminal error deterministic
